newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks finish lower in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks finish lower in dull trade.

text.p: Indian shares dropped in sluggish trade on Monday as support from local funds dried up coupled with major players staying on the sidelines, brokers said.
"Most of the domestic institutions were sitting quietly," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) fell 61.18 points or 1.94 percent to 3,099.34, a tad above the day's lowest mark of 3,098.0.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index lost 16.74 points or 1.84 percent to 892.05.

Analysts said they would expect the Reserve Bank of India (the central bank) to cut at least one percentage point in the cash reserve ratios of banks when it announces its monetary policy on Saturday.
This will help ease the market's tight liquidity situation and boost sentiment, they said.
"A lot is expected of the RBI this time," said K. Kannan, chairman and managing director of state-owned Bank of Baroda. "I have not seen expectations of such a high order before."
But others said an expected sharp fall in the first half profits of top private firm Reliance Industries -- due on Friday -- was bound to dampen the mood.

"In the shorter-term, the Reliance results may be more important than any cut in CRR," one analyst said. A Reuter poll forecast the petrochemical major's earnings would shrink 25 percent, hit by poor global polyester prices.
The Calcutta index was off 3.02 points to 420.79, while the Delhi Exchange index gained 0.08 points at 701.05 and the Madras index rose 15.56 points to 3,205.52.
